subject: Ownership pathways — exec signoff needed for ACME order form
messages:
From: Tom Hayes <t.hayes@acme.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify output ownership and training consent in MSA/Order Form

Sofia,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached are our redlines to the MSA + order form (see acme_redlines_v1.pdf). A few points we need explicit confirmation on before we can move to procurement:

- Does Redwood require a license to use customer-generated outputs for model training or improvements, or can a customer opt out entirely? If there is a license, can you provide the exact scope (e.g., anonymized improvements only, aggregation allowed)?
- We need confirmation that customer retains ownership of output (generated content) and that Redwood will not assert ownership or claim derivative rights.
- If Redwood intends to retain a feedback license, please state retention period for logs/feedback and whether the customer can request deletion.

We are trying to avoid open-ended training rights in the MSA. Elena (cc) is the procurement lead; she will need a definitive position to proceed to signature.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is pushing to close by next week.

Thanks,
Tom Hayes
Head of Legal — Acme Energy

Attachment: acme_redlines_v1.pdf (PDF, 78KB)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hayes <t.hayes@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 16:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify output ownership and training consent in MSA/Order Form

Tom —

Thanks for the redlines and the clear questions. High level response and path forward below; Laura and Connor are looped for legal/ops language.

Quick summary of options we can offer to Acme:

1) Default (recommended for speed): Customer retains ownership of outputs. Redwood receives a limited "feedback license" that allows use of anonymized/aggregated telemetry and feedback to improve the service (no attribution to Acme content). Retention: operational logs kept for up to 6 months; telemetry aggregated indefinitely at product-level only.

2) Enterprise opt-out: Customer can opt out of training/learning for an additional contractual fee and capacity considerations; opt-out requires express checkbox on order form and may impact troubleshooting capability.

3) Narrow training license: Redwood may use derivatives for safety/regression fixes only, explicitly excluding commercial model retraining for external model releases.

Next steps I propose:
- Laura to draft suggested redline language that captures (1) customer output ownership, (2) narrow feedback license, and (3) an opt-out path on the order form.
- Connor to confirm operational retention/deletion process for logs and provide a short runbook we can include as an exhibit.
- If ACME insists on full no-training/no-retention, we escalate to exec for signoff.

I've attached a short response doc for ACME that maps our proposals to their numbered redlines. Will await Laura's text.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Sales Strategy — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_response_v1.pdf (PDF, 34KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Tom Hayes <t.hayes@acme.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Aug 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify output ownership and training consent in MSA/Order Form

Sofia / Tom —

I reviewed ACME's redlines and drafted language we can push back with. Key proposed clauses (high-level):

- Output Ownership: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to Customer Content and Outputs generated by the Service when produced in response to Customer Content. Redwood shall not claim ownership of such Outputs."

- Limited Feedback License: "Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, revocable license to use anonymized, aggregated feedback and telemetry for the sole purpose of (a) improving the Service, (b) debugging, and (c) measuring quality. Such data shall not be used to create.models for resale or redistributed as training datasets to third parties."

- Retention & Deletion: "Operational logs/feedback will be retained for a period not to exceed six (6) months, subject to regulatory or troubleshooting exceptions. Customer may request deletion of logs associated with their account, which Redwood will complete within a commercially reasonable timeframe, documented in the Operations Runbook."

I attached a plain-text draft (legal-draft-output-license.txt) with redline-ready language. Two practical notes:
1) For strategic customers (ACME looks large), we should be willing to offer the enterprise opt-out but require exec-level approval and a commercial trade (fee or capacity constraints).
2) We need Connor to confirm the deletion SLA window and whether there are any technical limitations that would prevent a 30/60/90-day deletion commitment.

If Tom/Acme are OK with the limited feedback license language above, we can incorporate it into the MSA and update the order form to include the opt-out checkbox and a short explanation of operational impacts.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

Attachment: legal-draft-output-license.txt (TXT, 6KB)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 1 Sep 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify output ownership and training consent in MSA/Order Form

Team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. For ACME (strategic, large footprint), here is my directive so we have a single position to present:

- Accept customer ownership of Outputs.
- Offer a limited, revocable feedback license strictly for service improvements, safety fixes, and debugging. Prohibit use for model commercialization or resale.
- Retain operational logs for up to six (6) months; provide a documented deletion process (Connor, 30- to 90-day SLA suggestion).
- Provide an enterprise opt-out (no training/no feedback) option on the order form but only with exec signoff. The opt-out should be priced and may be conditioned on reduced support / extra runbook obligations.

Sofia — please consolidate Laura's draft into a single redline PDF and present this to ACME with a one-page executive note explaining the commercial impact of a full opt-out (we should ask for a fee or remove the one-click support guarantee). I want visibility before we accept any blanket no-training term.

-Markus
VP, Commercial Strategy — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Ownership pathways — exec signoff needed for ACME order form

Tom / Elena —

Thanks again for the redlines. Attached is a consolidated redline package (consolidated-redlines-for-acme.pdf) and a one-page executive note that explains the operational and commercial tradeoffs if ACME requires a full no-training opt-out.

Bottom line we can accept:
- ACME keeps ownership of Outputs.
- Redwood receives a limited, revocable feedback license for anonymized/aggregated telemetry and debugging that cannot be used for commercial model training or resale.
- Operational logs retained for up to six months; ACME may request deletion (we will comply per the Operations Runbook, 30–90 day completion window).
- If ACME requires a strict no-training/no-feedback clause, that is an enterprise opt-out that requires executive signoff and a commercial adjustment (fee or changes to support SLAs).

Next steps:
1) Please review the consolidated redlines and confirm whether you accept the limited feedback license language.
2) If you need the enterprise opt-out, confirm and we will route for exec approval and provide a commercial proposal.
3) If accepted, we'll prepare the final MSA + order form for signature and send a DocuSign link.

I copied Laura, Markus and Connor for transparency. If you'd like, we can do a 30-minute call tomorrow morning to walk through the changes.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Sales Strategy — Redwood Inference

Attachments: consolidated-redlines-for-acme.pdf (PDF, 48KB); redwood_response_v1.pdf (PDF, 34KB)
